APPENDIX ( Clause 0.2.1 )
DETERMINATION OF QUALITY INDEX

A
AND PRICE FIXATION

A-l. Within the limits of recommended levels of seaweed constituents and impurities, a formula has been designed by which one can calculate the quality index ( 01 ) of different seaweeds. The quality indices will be comparable for a particular type of phycocolloid produced by the same or different species. Content of phycocolloid ( percent ) x quality unit* Quality index = Total impurities?, percent A-2. Based on this index, different types of seaweeds can by compared and their market value fixed. For example, Gracilaria of Grade 1 quality having 35 percent agar, 125 g/cm2 gel strength and 9 percent impurities ( 7 percent moisture, 1 percent dirt, dust, etc, and 1 percent unwanted seaweeds ) will have a 01 of 486 while second grade Gracilaria having 25 percent agar. 70 g/cm2 gel strength and 18'5 percent impurities ( 14 percent moisture, 3 percent dirt, dust, etc and 1'5 percent unwanted seaweeds ) will have a 01 of 95. Both the quality indices are in the ratio of 5:l. Therefore, the market value of grade 1 Gracilaria should be five times that of Grade II quality.
*Gel strength ( g/cm2 ) for 1'5 percent agar at 27�C. *Adhered foreign materials like dirt, dust mud and sand or adulteration

Life history is usually with a free-living tetrasporophyte; sexual and sporophytic generations are generally isomorphic. Sporangia are usually in stichidial branchlets. B-l.2 Gracilaria - Gonimoblasts grow mostly from an auxiliary cell. vegetative cell. Texture is firmer, branches are essentially terete, multiaxial. Cover the container, vent hole, and autoclave for 3 hours at 121�C. Filter under pressure through glass-wool and a membrane filter ( 12 pm ). Keep the solution and the filter apparatus above 60�C. Pour the solution into shallow trays and allow it to gel at room temperature. Cut the gel into 2 cm strips and freeze. Thaw the gel at room temperature and filter off the free liquid with suction through an ordidary filter Wash the residue carefully with three 500-ml portions of paper covered with nylon mesh. distilled water and later on with 100 ml ethanol. Dry the agar overnight in an oven maintained at 6O'C and weigh. Store in a dry place. Triplicate samples shall be extracted in this way. The quantity of extractable agar, in these samples, shall not vary by more than 1 percent. Take the mean of triplicate quantity. C-2.2 Procedure

C-2.2.1 Take a 500-ml beaker and determine its weight. Weigh 3 g agar in this beaker. Add the required amount of distilled water to this beaker so that the combined weight of agar and water is Again weigh and adjust the combined weight of 200 g. Boil the water till agar dissolves completely. agar and water to 200 g with hot distilled water. Pour the agar solution into a 300-ml beaker of 5 cm diameter. Allow it to gel at 27�C (room temperature) for 15 hours before measuring gel strength. Prepare three sets in this way. Move the handle to right side for raising C-2.2.2 Fix the gel strength tester in a horizontal position. the weight adding device. Place the beaker, containing jelly, in such a way, that the lower surface of the weight adding device ( having 1 cm" base) should be in the centre of the beaker. Place an appropriate weight on the weight adding stand. Move the handle in the reverse direction and lower it gently until the end of the weight-adding device comes in contact with the jelly. Start the stop-watch as soon as the handle supporting the weight-adding device is separated from it and the weight is given to the jelly completely. Record the time from the beginning of the cracking of jelly till the entry of the end of the weight-adding device into jelly. If it penetrates within 20 seconds, change the measuring position and decrease the number of counter weights and repeat the measurement once again. If it does not penetrate after a lapse of 20 seconds, add another suitable weight and make the measurement as described earlier; repeat measurement till the maximum weight is obtained which takes 20 seconds for penetration. After measurement, add the weight of weight-adding device to the counter weight (weights added during measurement). This value is the strength of jelly ( in g/cm"). C-2.2.3 Take triplicate the mean of the triplicate C-3. Moisture measurements. measurements. The values should not vary by more than 1 percent. Calculate

Remove the insoluble matter from the cloth and keep it separately. through double fold muslin cloth. Remove the fragements of seaweeds, if present. Keep the filterate in another container. Again wash the same seaweeds with another one litre quantity of tap water. Separate the insolubles and filterate as described earlier. Combine the two insoluble matters into one. EXPLANATORY
Seaweeds are commercially utilized for the extraction
(food

NOTE
of chemicals
and

like alginic cosmetic

nate (textile and pharmaceutical grades) and agar have widespread usage in food, pharmaceutical

microbiological

grade).

The raw seaweeds also have a good potential

textile, for export.

confectionery,

acid, sodium algiThese products and other industries.

the

The availability of these seaweeds is less than the demand and, therefore, these are adulterated, common adulterants being moisture, dirt, mud, sand, etc, and low quality seaweeds of the same or different species. This standard has, therefore, been formulated to ensure availability of seaweeds of of the desired quality. Agar is used in microbial cultures, food, medicine drugs and pharmaceuticals, and in canning. It is also used as a stablizer, thickener and gelling agent and for sizing of fabrics, etc. Its use as an ingredient in waterproof paper, cloth and glue, as a clarifying agent in beer and wines and in the preparation of special diabetic foods is also very common. The following Indian Standards have been published on agar for different purposes: IS : 5707-1970 IS : 6850-1973 Agar, food grade Agar, microbiological grade assistance has been obtained from Central Salt

In the preparation of this standard; considerable and Marine Chemicals Research Institute, Bhavnagar.

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 5
